content: WELCOME TO COYLE HALL 2025-2026 Hall of the Year From unmatched traditions like The Regatta and Car Smash, to brand new events like Coyleween, Coyle Crushes, and the Coyle Ice Chapel Mass that drew national attention, this past year was momentous. This award marks the beginning of a new chapter for our dorm, and we couldn't have done it without the hard work of our residents, leadership team, and the support of the entire ND community. Thank you! Fishers of Men 1952 • 2025 Crew. Fishermen. Green Wave. Brothers. Coyle Hall has been known by many names over the years, but its legacy as one of the most iconic dorms at Notre Dame remains steadfast. Home to generations of proud residents, this brotherhood has long been one of the most tight-knit, spirited, and iconic on campus. From legendary events and unmatched camaraderie, to unforgettable haircuts and unwavering support, Coyle Hall isn't just a place for students to reside — it's a community of friendships, traditions, and countless memories that last a lifetime. Students come from every major, from every corner of the world and from every background, united by their shared identity as the Crew, and the bonds forged here are unlike any other. The mantra of "All are welcome" has carried through since the community's inception in 1952 as Fisher Hall, and it is even more true now, in the newest (and nicest) dorm on campus. The Cadillac, as the dorm is affectionately known, is a place for students to work, relax, study, grow, pray, but above all live at Notre Dame, and we couldn't be more happy to welcome you to our home! New Crew We can't wait to welcome you! title: Car Smash
description: Until the Car Smash Smashing Cars, Building Futures As one of Coyle Hall's signature and most beloved events, the Car Smash is a fun and casual way to raise money for St. Adalbert's. Every year, the …
content: Until the Car Smash Smashing Cars, Building Futures As one of Coyle Hall's signature and most beloved events, the Car Smash is a fun and casual way to raise money for St. Adalbert's. Every year, the Friday before a fall home game, Coyle Hall brings an old car out to Fieldhouse Mall. For a small donation, participants have the chance to smash the car with a hammer, and even bring home their own pieces as souvenirs. Not to mention, the opponents mascot is on the car, providing the perfect opportunity for fans to express their true feelings. With music, good food, fun vibes, and a lively atmosphere, the Car Smash is the best way to kick off a home game weekend and help support a great cause in the process! Thanks to everyone who came out to support the Car Smash this past year, we'll see you in the Fall!

Different from the usual dorm SYR (Screw Your Roommate), the Crunk is a chance for everyone in Coyle — and their dates — to embrace their inner '70s spirit with groovy fashion, flare pants, disco shirts, and (for the particularly brave) handlebar mustaches and long sideburns. Each year the dorm gathers in Stepan Center for a night of roller skating, dancing, and good old-fashioned '70s fun. Lace up your skates, dust off your bell-bottoms, and get ready to boogie. October 2, 2026 Stepan Center

title: Faith
description: A Community of Faith As a Catholic University, faith is the cornerstone of everything at Notre Dame. Nowhere is that more apparent than in the residence halls, especially Coyle Hall. Here, you'll find …
content: A Community of Faith As a Catholic University, faith is the cornerstone of everything at Notre Dame. Nowhere is that more apparent than in the residence halls, especially Coyle Hall. Here, you'll find a faith-filled community of students that support each other in their spiritual journeys through sacraments, prayer, and comraderie. Whether it's through daily mass in the chapel, weekly bible study, singing in the choir, special events during Lent and Advent, a quiet conversation, or even homemade ice cream, here, you'll find opportunities to not only grow in your faith, but build bonds with others as well. We say all are welcome in this place, and we mean it. Even if you aren't Catholic, you'll find a place here. Our choir, masses, events, chapel, and, of course, ice cream, are open to every student. Mass & Sacraments Chapel Mass Sun, Mon, Wed, Thur | 10 PM Come join us for mass in our own St. Paul's Chapel Adoration Wednesday | 9 - 9:50 PM Eucharistic Exposition, followed by Benediction Confession Wed | 9-9:50 PM | + By Appt Receive the sacrament of Reconciliation Ice Cream MassIce Cream Wednesday | 10 PM Enjoy Joey's homemade ice cream after Mass Get Involved Chapel Band Before & During Sun Mass Join our chapel band to sing or play. All talents and faiths are welcome! Bible Study Weekly Meetings Join one of our groups to deepen your understanding of Scripture and discuss relevant and meaningful topics. Volunteer During Any Mass Help with pastoral care and support by reading at Mass, altar serving, or being a Eucharistic minister. About The Priest About The Priest Fr. Greg Haake, CSC Fr. Greg is the priest in residence of Coyle Hall. Originally from Kansas City, MO, he now lives on the first floor of the dorm, and organizes various faith-based events, including all sacrament opportunities in Coyle. In addition to his duties in Coyle, Fr. Greg is also the University's Vice President for Mission Engagement and Church Affairs, as well as an Associate Professor of French in the Department of Romance Languages and Literatures. Ordained a priest in 2007, he received both a B.A. and an M.Div. from the University of Notre Dame and joined the faculty in 2015. He enjoys reading, watching movies, and is an avid Kansas City Chiefs fan. His favorite part of Coyle Hall is all of the students, of course! Contact Fr. Greg View Fr. Greg's Site

title: Family Weekend
description: Until Family Weekend Welcome Home, Coyle Families Welcome to campus, Coyle families! There is no better time to be under the Dome than the weekend the Irish take on Miami, and we cannot wait to share …
content: Until Family Weekend Welcome Home, Coyle Families Welcome to campus, Coyle families! There is no better time to be under the Dome than the weekend the Irish take on Miami, and we cannot wait to share it with you. Family Weekend is our chance to pull back the curtain on hall life, introduce you to the Crew, and celebrate the community your sons call home. Get ready for a weekend packed with game-day energy, gold-and-blue pride, and the warm Coyle spirit you have heard so much about. We kick things off Friday evening with an opening dinner, gathering the Crew and their families together to start the weekend on a full and festive note. From there, the campus and the game-day atmosphere take over, and you will have plenty of time to make memories with your son and other families. On Sunday morning, we come back together for a closing Mass, followed by a farewell brunch to send everyone off with full hearts and plates. We are so glad you are here, and we cannot wait to welcome you home to Coyle. November 6–8, 2026 Notre Dame vs. Miami

title: History
description: A Community of Comfort Built in 2026, Coyle Hall is one of the newest dorms on campus and features all the modern amenities and comforts you could ask for in a residence hall. Each floor has a …
content: A Community of Comfort Built in 2026, Coyle Hall is one of the newest dorms on campus and features all the modern amenities and comforts you could ask for in a residence hall. Each floor has a slightly different layout, but they each have all the essentials. You'll find spacious lounges, complete with a full kitchen with dishes and utensils, a TV, couches, study spaces, and more. The building is home to a variety of room types, including singles, doubles, three-room quads, and three-room six-man rooms, accessible singles and doubles, as well as apartments for hall staff. A small handful of doubles and singles have private bathrooms, but most rooms share between three large communal bathrooms, as well as some individual restrooms. The dorm is broken up into eight sections across the three floors. The first floor has two sections, while the second and third both have three. On the first floor, you'll also find a number of common spaces with game tables and ammenities for the whole dorm. The St. Paul's Chapel is located on the east side of the building, along with a spacious reading room and various study spaces. The first floor also houses common areas and lounges, as well as offices for hall staff and apartments for our rector as well as our Priest-in-Residence. In the basement, you'll find laundry and storage, our dorm gym, which features free weights, treadmill, cable machine, bench, squat rack, and more, plus our very own dorm sandwich shop, Ellie's Deli! Outside the dorm you'll find a large patio for communal gatherings and grilling, as well as a large green space for outdoor activities and games. Check out the images of various rooms in the building below, including common areas and typical rooms. Please note that the building is brand new, so some of these photos are renderings or were taken during construction. Dorm Floor Plans ResLife FAQs ResLife Dorm Page First Floor Common Areas The Chapel The Chapel of St. Paul, located on the first floor of Coyle Hall, is a holy place where the community gathers for Mass and prayer. Each week, the Crew come together to celebrate Sunday mass and daily mass throughout the week, complete with homemade ice cream on Wednesdays. The chapel is one of the largest on campus, and the piano and instruments inside enable the Coyle Dorm Choir to sing and perform at masses. In addition to masses and sacraments, the chapel is also a meeting place for the dorm community, where we come together to meet as a community. A rendering of the St. Paul Chapel Singles Single room on first/second floor Single room on the third floor Doubles Regular double on any floor Deluxe double with bay window Quads Quad center common room One of two quad side rooms Six Mans Six-man center common room One of two six-man side rooms Section Map The Hall is divided into 8 sections, with two on the first floor and three on the second and third. While Coyle Hall is proudly an anti-section culture dorm (which means we emphasize community across the entire dorm), sections are a nice supplement to dorm culture. Each section has an RA, residents across all four grades, and some even do special events. This map shows the naming layout for each section. The part of the building and the floor combine to make section names (ie. 2B is the middle section on the second floor). The first floor has two sections, 1A and 1B, while the second and third floors each have three sections, A, B, and C.

title: History
description: A Community of Tradition Building a Legacy The story of Coyle began back in 1952, when Sally Fisher donated the money to build Fisher Hall in memory of her late husband, Fred Fisher, a former member …
content: A Community of Tradition Building a Legacy The story of Coyle began back in 1952, when Sally Fisher donated the money to build Fisher Hall in memory of her late husband, Fred Fisher, a former member of the Board of Trustees. The dorm was originally constructed to house 156 seniors, and had a large number of single rooms. At the time, it was one of the first dorms at Notre Dame to host newer ammenities like shared common lounges, and it was home to the original St. Paul's Chapel. The dorm was renovated a number of times, most notably in the Summer of 2001. Throughout its glorious existence, the Fisher/Coyle Community has been home to some of Notre Dame's most legendary alumni. NBA stars LaPhonso Ellis ’92 and Orlando Woolridge ’81 once walked these halls, as well as the one and only Regis Philbin ’53. In addition to the legend among legends, Joe Montana ’79, hundreds of students, athletes, businessmen, engineers, scientists, artists, and leaders have called Fisher Hall home. The original home of the Coyle Community, Fisher Hall, before its demolition in 2024 The temporary home of the Coyle Community, Zahm Hall, during the 2024-2025 and 2025-2026 school years Keeping it Alive In 2024, the University announced that the old Fisher Hall would be demolished to make way for a new residence hall, Coyle Hall, named in honor of John and Jill Coyle. It was announced that, while the new building was constructred, the community would live in Zahm Hall under the name "Fisher Community in Zahm Hall". Cast out of their beloved South Quad home, the community embraced the change, determined to keep the spirit of Fisher alive. Relationships with new dorms were developed, and the community claimed a new dorm table, this time in North Dining Hall. Life in Zahm brought small upgrades as well, with an increased number of small lounges, larger rooms, a larger chapel, and a newly renovated basement and gym. Still, the community longed to be back in their original home, and excitement for the new building grew. Moving Forward In Summer 2025, the community adopted a new name for the year: "Coyle Community in Zahm Hall". This was the start of a new relationship between the dorm community and the donors, John and Jill, and offered the chance to make new traditions and memories. Many traditions, like Fisher Funk, were rebranded to Coyle equivilents, like the Coyle Crunk, and many new traditions were started, all bearing names that began with 'C'. Finally, in Fall 2026, the community moved into the brand new Coyle Hall. Featuring a spacious lounges, kitchens on every floor, new study areas, six-man rooms, a newer, taller, and bigger St. Paul's Chapel, and, at long last, air conditioning. Throughout its storied history, the dorm has kept the same spirit of brotherhood, community, and tradition, and, now as the brand new Coyle Hall, that spirit is stronger than ever. A rendering of the front of Coyle Hall, viewed from across South Quad

title: Incoming Students

content: 00 Days 00 Hours 00 Minutes 00 Seconds Until Welcome Weekend Welcome Incoming Students! Congrats! You've been chosen to become part of the best dorm on campus. We couldn't be more excited to welcome you to your new home, and we hope you're looking forward to it as much as we are. This isn’t just where you’ll live—it’s where you’ll grow, laugh, make unforgettable memories, and find a community that truly feels like home. Get excited for a warm welcome, incredible people, and the beginning of something truly special. We can’t wait to meet you and see everything you’ll bring to our community. As you prepare for move in, check out the resources we've compiled below to help you get ready. Below, you'll find room information, packing lists, and other important details to help you make the most of your time in Coyle. Additionally, take some time to reach out to your roomate(s) and get to know them (you will be living together after all). Hopefully, you'll become good friends! Coyle Hall Room Guide Residential Life FAQs Floor Plans Welcome Weekend What's in a Room All first-year students are placed in standard size doubles (non-deluxe), or accessible singles/doubles if they have an accommodation. Transfer students may be placed in any type of room, though it is usually a standard double or single. All rooms have windows, sinks, A/C and a standard set of furniture. Accessible rooms may have private bathrooms as well as accessible furniture. Check out standard room furnishings below: Rooms Come With: Bed & Mattress 1 Each Per Person Ladder As Needed Closet 1 Per Person 2 Drawers 1 Set Per Person Desk & Chair 1 Each Per Person Sink 1 Per Room Mirror Cabinet 1 Each Per Room Trash & Recyle 2 Bins Per Room Beds can be lofted, raised, bunked, or just placed. Ladders are available for each high bed if needed. Sinks are on a cabinet with shelves below and a medicine cabinet and mirror above. Things to Bring, Pack, or Buy This is an incomplete list, but here are some common items to consider having in your room. You'll want to coordinate with your roommate, especially with bigger items, so you don't end up bringing two of everything. There are plenty of stores in the South Bend area, including Target, Costco, and Walmart, if you'd rather buy stuff after move-in. Feel free to have items delivered to your room, but they must arrive after move-in or they won't be accepted. What You'll Need Pillow & Sheets Twin XL Size, 2 sets is nice Fans Box & Oscillating Fans Are Common Toiletries Soap, Shaving, Deodorant, etc. Shower Caddy For Carrying Shower Supplies Laundry Supplies Bag, Detergent, Softener, etc Medication Over The Counter & Prescription Clothing Casual & Formal (Bring a Suit) Hangers Closet Organizers Are Helpful Too Shoes Casual, Athletic, Formal, & Boots! Shower Shoes Incredibly Important! Laptop Many Students Also Use Tablets Extension Cords Lots of Outlets, Tucked Away Power Strips Make Sure It Has Surge Protection Towels Full-Size, Hand, & Washcloths School Supplies Pens, Notebooks, Calculator, etc. ID/License + Any Neccessary Documentation What You'll Want Minifridge No Bigger Than 5 cu. ft Rug(s) Better Than Tile, Sizes Vary Television Streaming Works Great Couch/Futon Comfy & Handy For Guests What's Not Allowed Microwaves A/C Units Large Fridges Humidifiers Lighted Candles Appliances Illegal Drugs Weapons Microwaves A/C Units Large Fridges Humidifiers Lighted Candles Appliances Illegal Drugs Weapons

content: A Community of Activity Though the community has called several buildings home over the years, our roots have always been on South Quad, otherwise known as the longest quad in America. Near the heart of campus, the dorm is nestled between classic Notre Dame landmarks, with South Dining Hall right next door and the Rock only steps away. Next door lies Grojean Hall, to the south are Duncan, McGlinn, and O'Neill Halls, and through the Lyons Arch you can see the beautiful St. Mary's Lake. Whether it's playing spikeball or hacky sack on the quad, jogging around the lakes, joining a pickup game at the Bookstore Courts, or stopping by the dining hall for a quick bite, Coyle Hall is close to the action and near everything you need to be succesful, have fun, and enjoy college life! title: St. Adalbert's
description: A Community of Care Coyle Hall has been blessed with the opportunity to give back to the South Bend community by supporting St. Adalbert's Catholic School. Each year, the dorm raises funds through our …
content: A Community of Care Coyle Hall has been blessed with the opportunity to give back to the South Bend community by supporting St. Adalbert's Catholic School. Each year, the dorm raises funds through our signature events, including the Regatta, Car Smash, and more. Money raised by the dorm goes directly to the school, helping to fund improvement projects, school programs, and other initiatives benefiting students in our community. Beyond the money, the Crew show up in person, volunteering and spending time supporting the school and its students. The relationship with St. Adalbert's is built on the qualities of community and charity that are central to Coyle Hall, and it is the foundation of everything we do as a dorm. Thousands Of Dollars Raised Through the Regatta, Car Smash, and other fundraisers Hundreds Of Hours Volunteering Tutoring, mentoring, teaching, and playing with students Dozens Of School Improvements Made possible through partnership and fundraising About the School About St. Adalbert's St. Adalbert's is a Catholic School located in western South Bend and operating by the Congregation of Holy Cross. As both are Holy Cross schools, Notre Dame and St. Adalbert's share a special relationship, one that Coyle Hall is proud to be a part of. Priests from both institutions frequently visit each other and collaborate across education, ministry, and service. St. Adalbert's has over 200 students ranging from Pre-K to 8th grade. The school and parish are home to large Hispanic and Latino communities, and the school offers bilingual education and support for students. The school opened in 1911 and was originally ministered by the Felician Sisters from Detroit. In 2003, ministry of the parish and school was transferred to the Congregation of Holy Cross, where it has remained through today. Learn About the School

title: The Regatta
description: Ya Gotta Regatta The Regatta: A Timeless Classic for Over 25 Years The Regatta is known as one of the largest, most successful, and most outrageous signature event on campus. Each year, Coyle Hall …
content: Ya Gotta Regatta The Regatta: A Timeless Classic for Over 25 Years The Regatta is known as one of the largest, most successful, and most outrageous signature event on campus. Each year, Coyle Hall kicks off spring by hosting a multi-heat boat-racing tournament on St. Mary’s Lake, and each boat entered must be home-made. Most dorms field at least one boat, and other non-dorm boats, like the ND Concrete Canoe team, compete as well. Past years have seen everything from giant pirate ships and floundering Styrofoam rafts to floating basketball courts and tv lounges, and each year brings something new. The Regatta draws over a thousand participants and spectators, with food, merch, music, live broadcasting, and great vibes all day. In fact, it's so popular that it even made ESPN's Top 100 College Events! Of course, we forgot to mention the infamous Regatta Hawk, a legendary tradition known across campus, where Fresh Crew all shave their hair into mohawks to promote dorm unity and the spirit of the Regatta. Thanks to everyone who came out to support the Regatta this year, it was a huge success! See you in April next year! Broadcast Replay

title: Joey Quinones
